speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Following your report of right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision, please describe exactly how your right leg is positioned now and whether you can move it at all. Also, did you hear a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of impact?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you bear weight on the right leg, and does moving your hip into flexion or abduction reproduce the severe groin pain? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_XRay.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Anterior Hip Dislocation. The mechanism of a rear-end collision causing the passenger to thrust their hip backward against the seat while the leg is flexed, combined with immediate groin pain, inability to bear weight, and abnormal positioning (often externally rotated), is classic for this injury. Please request an immediate Hip X-Ray series (AP and Lateral) to confirm the diagnosis before attempting reduction.
